Aceh is the northern tip of Sumatra, at the entrance to the Strait of Malacca. The map shows it from 1279 to 1600. Before the Aceh Sultanate, the coast held small port kingdoms such as Samudera Pasai, the first Muslim sultanate in the region, whose ruler Malik al-Salih died in 1297. Ibn Battuta stopped at Pasai in 1345.

The Aceh Sultanate was founded around 1496. It grew fast after Portugal took Malacca in 1511, as Muslim traders moved their business to its ports. Aceh sold pepper to the Middle East and fought the Portuguese for decades. In the 1560s it sought help from the Ottoman Empire, which sent cannon and gunners.

It reached its peak under Iskandar Muda, from 1607 to 1636, and was known as a centre of Islamic learning. The Dutch fought a long, brutal Aceh War from 1873 to absorb it into their colony.
